summary: Focused follow-up on ep 44 (FS ep 20 'Gotta Buy a Step Stool'). Verdict: the batch-14 anime-original call STANDS — ep 44 adapts no manga chapter, and the doubt is resolved with positive evidence: the previously-unclaimed range 169-171 turns out to be the Kyuu chapters (Kyuu is a lop-eared rabbit, on all three covers and in every character list for 169-171), and Kyuu never physically appears in the anime (fandom infobox: anime = 'Episode 29 (image on TV)'), so that range is cut, not relocated into ep 44 — the rat-base/frame-up/kines material matches no chapter title or character list anywhere in 161-179, and the MAL ep-8 thread's viewer descriptions (framing, planted kines, sewer rat base, Gosha stalking Haru) carry zero chapter citations. One real gain elsewhere: ep 43 DOES adapt ch 166 in part — its opening Festival of Odd Souls (turtle praying to the frozen Brachiosaurus bone) is ch-166 material per the fandom Holidays page's two ch-166 citations, corroborated by es-fandom's ch-166 character list (herbivore crowd + Haru, with Legoshi only in her imagination and Melon in flashback) — so ep 43's list gains a leading '166 (part)'. Bonus range fact: the manga's real first kiss is ch 173 (manga-reader post, April 2020), which the anime cuts from its ep-47 '172-176 abridged' span and relocates as an anime-original public kiss in the ep-48 finale; ep 44's kiss-deferral scene is therefore original writing, at most a motif-level echo of ch 166's Haru-imagines-Legoshi beat (the ep title 'Gotta Buy a Step Stool' / 踏み台を買わなきゃ pairs with ch 166's Haru-stature title 身の丈の運命わたしにください, but no source confirms the line exists in the chapter).

anchors.note: Adds ch 166 (part) to the stored 150-151 record: the episode opens with the Festival of Odd Souls, whose worship of the frozen Brachiosaurus bone / holy water / amulet offerings is cited to Chapter 166 twice on the fandom Holidays page, and Anime Rants ep-19 review confirms the anime staged exactly that detail (turtle praying to the dinosaur deity) as the episode's opening; es-fandom's Capítulo 166 character list (herbivore crowd, Haru, Legoshi only in Haru's imagination, Melon in flashback) corroborates that 166 is the festival/Haru chapter. Only the festival/Haru side of 166 is usable — its Louis-inherits-the-conglomerate half (Ogma in a funeral photo) is contradicted by the anime's Ogma-survives divergence. START stays 150 (first mainline chapter; 166 is a graft leading the list, same convention as eps 45/47). END 151, vol 17, resume 156 all unchanged.

zone_level_only.best_bound: No chapter is adapted; the batch-14 anime-original call is CONFIRMED, now with positive range evidence rather than stub silence. Every ep-44 thread is original: Legoshi framed for the interspecies murders (the murders plot itself is anime-original, eps 37-43), kines planted in his room, police questioning his connections, the rat informant + sewer rat base (no rats in any chapter title/character list 161-179; the manga's rat lore, ch 138, was already used in ep 26), Louis's 'Live Together' channel, Kuroe/Ogma artificial-meat Zoolympics scene (Kuroe is anime-exclusive, Ogma-alive is a divergence), and Gosha stalking/guarding Haru (setup for ep 45's ch-189 graft). The candidate range 169-171 is disproven: those are the Kyuu chapters (169 'Who Says He's Just a Giraffe Meat Sausage?', 170 'Infinite Table Manners', 171 'Blackmail While Staring at Her Lips' — Kyuu on all three covers, in all character lists), and Kyuu never appears in the anime (infobox anime field: 'Episode 29 (image on TV)'), so 169-171 are cut outright, not relocated. The park kiss-deferral is also original: the manga's actual first kiss is ch 173 (manga-reader post dated April 2020), which the anime removes from ep 47's 172-176 abridgement and restages as an anime-original public kiss in the ep-48 finale.

flags_for_sean: Ep 44 doubt RESOLVED: anime-only-canon confirmed. The suspicion that the frame-up/rat-base material adapted the unclaimed ~169-175 range is disproven — 169-171 are the Kyuu chapters (lop-eared rabbit, on every cover/character list in that span) and Kyuu never appears in the anime (fandom infobox: 'Episode 29 (image on TV)' only); 172-176 already belong to ep 47. So the Final Season's unadapted pockets in the 160s-170s are: 165 (Ogma's death — contradicted by the anime's Ogma-survives divergence), most of 166 (only the festival exposition is used, in ep 43), and 169-171 (Kyuu, cut with the rest of her thread 159-161/186).

Motif watch, not an anchor: ep 44's title 'Gotta Buy a Step Stool' (踏み台を買わなきゃ) pairs suspiciously with ch 166's title 'Give Me the Destiny I Deserve' (身の丈の運命わたしにください — 'a fate matching my stature'), and es-fandom confirms ch 166 contains Haru imagining Legoshi (with a Melon flashback). If a manga reader ever confirms ch 166 contains Haru's step-stool/kiss-fantasy line, ep 44's park scene would earn '166 (part)' and the type would flip to mixed. Current evidence says the scene as aired (self-defense tools, rat informant, Legoshi's deferral speech) is original — chapter synopses 165-185 are still stubs, so this stays a flag.

Kiss divergence worth an in-app note: the manga's first real Legoshi-Haru kiss is ch 173 ('Thawing ××××', the snowmelt kiss — manga-reader post from April 2020, '173 chapters later... finally kiss for real'), inside ep 47's '172-176 (abridged)' span; the anime cuts it there and instead stages an anime-original public kiss in the ep-48 finale (Haru kisses Legoshi in front of the Zoolympics crowd after the mayor fight, per Anime Rants ep-24 review). Ep 44's deferral scene ('no kiss until Melon is behind bars') is the anime's setup for that relocation.
